name: Tawang Monastery (Gaden Namgyal Lhatse)
description: Largest monastery in India and second-largest in the world, founded in 1681 by Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso. Gelug school complex overlooking Tawang Chu valley with golden Buddha statue, ancient scriptures, and home to hundreds of monks. Major spiritual and cultural landmark of Tawang.
facts: Founded 1680-1681 by Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso
About 3 km from Tawang town centre

name: Sela Pass
description: High-altitude mountain pass at 4,170 m on the Tawang–West Kameng border, gateway to Tawang on NH-13. Often snow-covered with nearby Sela Lake (Paradise Lake); dramatic scenic drive through Eastern Himalayas. Sela Tunnel (opened 2024) improves year-round access.
facts: On border of Tawang and West Kameng districts

name: Sangetsar Tso (Madhuri Lake)
description: High-altitude lake at about 3,708 m on the road to Bum La, formed by a 1950s earthquake that submerged trees whose trunks still rise from the water. Popularly called Madhuri Lake after a Bollywood shoot; striking photogenic spot amid Himalayan peaks.
facts: Also known as Madhuri Lake or Shonga-tser Lake

name: Nuranang Falls (Jang Falls)
description: 100 m high curtain waterfall near Jang town on the Tawang–Bomdila road, also known as Bong Bong Falls. Originates from northern slopes of Sela Pass and joins Tawang River; small hydel plant at base. Popular scenic stop with possible rainbows.
facts: About 2 km from Jang, 40 km from Tawang
Also called Jung Falls or Bong Bong Falls
Nuranang River from Sela Pass slopes

name: Bum La Pass
description: High-altitude border pass at about 4,600 m on the India–China Line of Actual Control, 37 km from Tawang. Historic 1962 war site and current Border Personnel Meeting point. Requires special DC and army permit; Indian nationals only. Stark alpine views.
facts: Special permit from DC office + army
1962 war battle site and BPM point

name: Urgelling Monastery
description: Historic Buddhist monastery about 3–5 km from Tawang town, birthplace of the 6th Dalai Lama Tsangyang Gyatso (born 1683). Founded in the 15th century; smaller and quieter than Tawang Monastery, important for Tibetan Buddhist history.

name: Tawang War Memorial
description: Chorten-style memorial in Tawang town honouring Indian soldiers who died in the 1962 Sino-Indian War. Features engraved names, prayer flags, and peaceful hilltop setting with views over the valley. Also known as Namgyal Chorten.

name: Jaswant Garh Memorial
description: War memorial on NH-13 near Nuranang honouring Rifleman Jaswant Singh Rawat of 4 Garhwal Rifles, who held position for days in 1962 and received Maha Vir Chakra posthumously. Maintained by army with bunker, exhibits and living tradition of service.
facts: Honours Rifleman Jaswant Singh Rawat MVC (P)
About 25–52 km from Tawang on NH-13

name: Pankang Teng Tso (PT Tso)
description: High-altitude glacial lake about 16–18 km from Tawang on the road to Bum La Pass. Crystal-clear or frozen waters reflecting peaks; sacred to Monpa people and popular stop with rhododendron surroundings. Requires Bum La road permit.
facts: Also called PT Tso or Panga Teng Tso
On Bum La road; permit needed

name: Tawang Town
description: District headquarters and main tourist base at about 3,048 m, gateway for monastery, passes and lakes. Monpa cultural hub with markets, hotels and administrative offices for permits. Surrounded by peaks and close to Bhutan and China borders.
facts: Road access via Sela Pass/Tunnel from Tezpur

name: Zemithang
description: Remote border village (also Pangchen) about 85–90 km west of Tawang near Bhutan, where the 14th Dalai Lama first entered India in 1959. Lower elevation with terraced fields, prayer flags and black-necked crane wintering area. Base for Gorsam Chorten.
facts: About 85–90 km from Tawang via Lumla
Entry point of 14th Dalai Lama in 1959
ILP sufficient; no extra army permit

name: Chakzam Bridge
description: Historic 15th-century iron chain bridge across the Tawang-Chu River near Mukto, attributed to Tangton Gyalpo. Rare surviving example of traditional Tibetan engineering still functional for local use; short detour from main Tawang route.
facts: About 20–25 km from Tawang near Mukto
